ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure there is a positively charged H3N-H fragment, namely the ammonium ion form; below is a nitrogen-containing organic skeleton, where the nitrogen atom is connected to the alkenyl fragment on the right and to the saturated carbon chain on the left, the chain has multiple R substituents, there is a C=C double bond at the lower right, and there is a carbonyl at the upper right. Several curved arrows are also drawn in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the curved arrows, this structure should be read according to ordinary connectivity as two unconnected components. The upper H3N-H positively charged fragment is written as [NH4+]. In the lower organic fragment, each R group is represented by the wildcard atom *. According to the specified method, tracing starts from the right R-substituted alkene, passes through C=C to N, and then through the saturated carbon chain to the carbonyl, which can be written as */C=C/NC(C*)C(*)C(C)=O. The alkene configuration is represented by /C=C/. The two unconnected components are connected with a dot, therefore the overall SMILES is */C=C/NC(C*)C(*)C(C)=O.[NH4+].
